article.title: Mark your calendars: A Googlebook ‘celebration’ is happening next month
article.summary: Credit: Google TL;DR Google will be hosting an event in New York City next month. This event will be where the company shows off the first wave of Googlebooks. The show, called Opening Night, will take place on October 5. On Monday, Google finally revealed when you’ll be able to start pre-ordering its new category of laptops, known as Googlebooks. The company has revealed hardly any information about this new hardware to date. But we won’t have to wait that much longer to finally start getting some details. According to Engadget , Google has begun sending out invites to an upcoming event called “Opening Night.” The event is scheduled for October 5 and will take place in New York City. article.title: AWS agents will suggest your new flights. Code decides what gets booked.
article.summary: AWS published a new Step Functions pattern this week that gives AI agents a role in airline rebooking while keeping reservation changes and payments under code’s control. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore agents suggest new itineraries and draft compensation messages after a flight disruption. Deterministic steps in the workflow then validate those proposals before changing any reservation or issuing payment. article.title: Google Home will soon let you swap Gemini for Claude, or another agent of your choice
article.summary: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google has announced an MCP connector for Google Home. It will let users monitor and control their smart homes through other AI chatbots or integrate them into agentic workflows. The MCP will soon be available in early access to Google Home Premium Advanced in the US. Last October, the Google Home platform received a significant upgrade with Gemini in copious amounts. One of the key new functionalities is Ask Home, which lets users talk to the app using natural language queries, and Google is even working on the ability to include media to make searches even better .
